# Tools: Webhooks, exports and analytics bridge

Cards for every tool this skill names. Rendered authority: [A] call · [C] confirm first · [O] owner order only.

## Owned

### `list_webhook_subscriptions` [A] · read · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the outgoing webhook subscriptions (external URLs that receive LPM events) of a workspace or project.
Use when: Before creating a subscription, to avoid a duplicate for the same URL.; Getting a subscriptionId to update, pause, test, delete or inspect deliveries.; Auditing which external endpoints receive workspace data.    Avoid when: You need delivery results: use list_webhook_deliveries.; You are looking for commit-to-activity linking (LPM-Activity trailers): that is a built-in GitHub webhook, not a subscription.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Always pass it (see errors). |
| projectId | no | list_projects -> id | Narrow to one project's subscriptions. |
Preconditions: API key profile includes sensitive admin tools (full or custom).; Caller can read the workspace (and project) of each subscription returned.
Returns: JSON array sorted by createdAt desc: [{id, workspaceId, projectId, name, url, secret: null, secretPreview, events[], status (active|paused|revoked), createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt}]. Use id as subscriptionId.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'You do not have access to this project' or 'Project <id> not found' when called without filters | Some subscription belongs to a project you cannot read and fails the whole call. Call again with workspaceId (and projectId). |
| Tool not found / access denied | The key profile excludes sensitive admin tools. Call get_mcp_connection_info; ask the owner. |
Gotchas:
- The secret is never returned (secretPreview is masked); never ask the user to paste it into chat to 'check' it.
- The server scans all subscriptions and filters afterwards, so always filter by workspaceId.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `update_webhook_subscription`, `test_webhook_subscription`, `list_webhook_deliveries`

### `create_webhook_subscription` [O] · write · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Registers an external URL to which LPM will POST signed JSON events for a workspace (optionally limited to one project).
Use when: The workspace owner explicitly asks to send LPM events to an external system (CI, chat bot, data sync) and provides the URL and shared secret.    Avoid when: A subscription for that URL already exists: use update_webhook_subscription.; You want commit-to-activity linking: use the LPM-Activity commit trailer (built-in GitHub webhook), no subscription needed.; You want WhatsApp intake: that is the operational-intake EvolutionAPI channel, not an outgoing webhook.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id |  |
| projectId | no | list_workspace_projects -> id | Must belong to workspaceId. Omit for the whole workspace. |
| name | yes | user | Non-empty. |
| url | yes | user | Full endpoint URL (https). Not validated by the server. |
| secret | yes | user | Shared secret given by the owner. Never invent it, never print or log it. |
| events | yes | constant | Array, at least one of: issue_created, issue_updated, issue_started, issue_completed, issue_canceled, issue_reopened, issue_priority_changed, requirement_created, requirement_updated, comment_added, export.completed, or '*' for all. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active member with role owner or admin.; API key profile includes sensitive admin tools (full or custom).; The owner explicitly asked for it and supplied the URL and secret.
Returns: Subscription object {id, workspaceId, projectId, name, url, secret: null, secretPreview, events (deduplicated, sorted), status: 'active', createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt}. id is the subscriptionId.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'You do not have permission to manage this workspace' | Only a workspace owner/admin can do this. Stop and tell the user. |
| 'Project does not belong to the selected workspace' | Use a projectId from list_workspace_projects(workspaceId). |
| 'Webhook name is required' / 'Webhook url is required' / 'Webhook secret is required' | Ask the user for the missing value. |
| 'Select at least one webhook event' | Pass at least one event name from the list in inputs. |
Gotchas:
- Event names are not validated: a typo (e.g. 'issue.created') is accepted and never fires.
- The subscription is active immediately and starts sending workspace data (titles, comments, export metadata) to the URL.
- Each POST body is {id, eventType, workspaceId, projectId, timestamp, payload} with headers X-LPM-Event, X-LPM-Delivery-Id and X-LPM-Signature = hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using the secret.
- Failed deliveries retry up to 5 attempts (30 s doubling, max 30 min) and are then dead-lettered.
- A second call creates a second subscription (double deliveries); check list_webhook_subscriptions first.
- Then run test_webhook_subscription.
Pairs with: `list_webhook_subscriptions`, `test_webhook_subscription`, `list_webhook_deliveries`

### `update_webhook_subscription` [O] · write · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Changes an existing webhook subscription's name, URL, secret, events, or pauses/reactivates it.
Use when: The owner asks to pause (status paused) or resume (status active) a subscription.; The owner gives a new URL or rotates the shared secret.; The owner wants to change which events are sent.    Avoid when: Moving the subscription to another workspace or project: not supported; delete_webhook_subscription then create_webhook_subscription.; Removing it for good: use delete_webhook_subscription (pausing is usually better).
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| subscriptionId | yes | list_webhook_subscriptions -> id |  |
| name | no | user | Empty string is ignored. |
| url | no | user | Empty string is ignored. |
| secret | no | user | New shared secret from the owner. Never print it. |
| events | no | constant | Replaces the whole set; at least one (same names as create_webhook_subscription). |
| status | no | constant | active \| paused |
Preconditions: Caller is the owner or an owner/admin member of the subscription's workspace.; API key profile includes sensitive admin tools.; The owner explicitly asked for the change.
Returns: Updated subscription object {id, name, url, secret: null, secretPreview, events, status, updatedAt, ...}.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'Webhook subscription not found' | Re-list with list_webhook_subscriptions(workspaceId). |
| 'You do not have permission to manage this workspace' | Only a workspace owner/admin can do this. Stop and tell the user. |
| 'Select at least one webhook event' | events cannot be empty; to stop all events use status paused. |
| 'Webhook subscription status is invalid' | Use active or paused. |
Gotchas:
- Events that happen while paused are never queued (lost, not replayed); deliveries already queued are dead-lettered with 'Subscription is not active.'.
- A new secret replaces the old one immediately (no overlap): the receiver must switch at the same moment.
- Fields cannot be cleared with empty strings.
Pairs with: `list_webhook_subscriptions`, `test_webhook_subscription`, `list_webhook_deliveries`

### `delete_webhook_subscription` [O] · destructive · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Permanently deletes a webhook subscription so LPM stops sending events to its URL.
Use when: The owner explicitly asks to remove an integration for good.    Avoid when: A temporary stop: use update_webhook_subscription with status paused.; Changing URL, secret or events: use update_webhook_subscription.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| subscriptionId | yes | list_webhook_subscriptions -> id |  |
Preconditions: Caller is the owner or an owner/admin member of the subscription's workspace.; API key profile includes sensitive admin tools.; The owner explicitly confirmed the deletion of this subscription (name + URL).
Returns: Plain text (not JSON): 'Webhook subscription <id> deleted successfully.'
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'Webhook subscription not found' | Already deleted or wrong id; re-list with list_webhook_subscriptions(workspaceId). Do not retry. |
| 'You do not have permission to manage this workspace' | Only a workspace owner/admin can do this. Stop and tell the user. |
Gotchas:
- Hard delete: the stored secret is lost and cannot be recovered; recreating needs the secret again.
- Deliveries still queued are dead-lettered with 'Subscription removed before delivery.'.
- Past deliveries remain visible in list_webhook_deliveries.
Pairs with: `list_webhook_subscriptions`

### `test_webhook_subscription` [C] · write · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Queues one 'system.test' POST to a subscription's URL so you can check that the endpoint receives it and verifies the signature.
Use when: Right after create_webhook_subscription or after changing the URL/secret.; Diagnosing an endpoint whose deliveries are failing.    Avoid when: You want to see delivery results: use list_webhook_deliveries.; The subscription is paused: the test will be dead-lettered; resume it first with update_webhook_subscription (if the owner agrees).
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| subscriptionId | yes | list_webhook_subscriptions -> id (or create_webhook_subscription -> id) |  |
Preconditions: Caller is the owner or an owner/admin member of the subscription's workspace.; API key profile includes sensitive admin tools.; The user agreed to send a test request to the external URL.
Returns: Plain text (not JSON): 'Webhook subscription <id> test queued successfully.' No delivery id is returned.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'Webhook subscription not found' | Re-list with list_webhook_subscriptions(workspaceId). |
| 'You do not have permission to manage this workspace' | Only a workspace owner/admin can do this. Stop and tell the user. |
Gotchas:
- Asynchronous: a background worker sends it.
- Then call list_webhook_deliveries(subscriptionId) and look for eventType 'system.test': status delivered = OK; lastError (e.g. 'Webhook endpoint responded with 401') = receiver problem.
- It is sent even if 'system.test' is not in the subscription's events.
- Payload: {type: 'system.test', timestamp, subscriptionId, workspaceId, projectId, source: 'lpm-test'}.
- Each call sends another POST.
Pairs with: `create_webhook_subscription`, `list_webhook_deliveries`

### `list_webhook_deliveries` [A] · read · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists recent outgoing webhook deliveries with their status, attempt count and last error.
Use when: Checking the result of test_webhook_subscription.; Diagnosing why an external system did not receive LPM events.; Auditing which events were sent to a subscription.    Avoid when: You need the subscription configuration: use list_webhook_subscriptions.; You need the event payload content: not returned here.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Pass it or subscriptionId (see errors). |
| projectId | no | list_projects -> id | Filter. |
| subscriptionId | no | list_webhook_subscriptions -> id | Filter. |
| limitCount | no | constant | Default 20, max 100. |
Preconditions: API key profile includes sensitive admin tools (full or custom).; Caller can read the workspace/project of each delivery returned.
Returns: JSON array sorted by createdAt desc: [{id, subscriptionId, workspaceId, projectId, eventType, status (queued|running|delivered|dead-lettered), correlationId, attemptCount, nextAttemptAt, deliveredAt, lastError, createdAt, updatedAt}].
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'You do not have access to this project' or 'Project <id> not found' when called without filters | A delivery of a project you cannot read fails the whole call. Call again with workspaceId or subscriptionId. |
| Tool not found / access denied | The key profile excludes sensitive admin tools. Call get_mcp_connection_info; ask the owner. |
Gotchas:
- queued with a future nextAttemptAt = waiting for retry (max 5 attempts, 30 s doubling up to 30 min).
- dead-lettered = given up (endpoint failing, subscription paused or deleted); there is no redeliver tool: fix the endpoint, then test_webhook_subscription again.
- lastError 'Webhook endpoint responded with 401/403' usually means the receiver rejects the signature/secret.
- The server scans all deliveries and filters afterwards, so always filter.
Pairs with: `test_webhook_subscription`, `update_webhook_subscription`

### `list_export_requests` [A] · read · KEY · profiles: full, read-only, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the data-export jobs the caller requested, newest first, with their status.
Use when: Polling an export created with create_export_request until it is completed or failed.; Checking whether an export is already queued or running before creating another.    Avoid when: You need the exported data itself: the zip can only be downloaded in the LPM web app (Settings); MCP gives no download link.; You need exports requested by other users: not available.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Filter. |
| projectId | no | list_projects -> id | Filter. |
| limitCount | no | constant | Default 20 newest. |
Preconditions: Authenticated caller.
Returns: JSON array sorted by createdAt desc: [{id, scope, workspaceId, projectId, requestedBy, status (queued|running|completed|failed|expired), format 'json-zip', filters, storagePath, signedUrlExpiresAt, recordCounts, checksum (sha256), correlationId, createdAt, updatedAt, completedAt, failedAt, errorMessage}].
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| status 'failed' with errorMessage | Report errorMessage to the user; create a new export only if they ask. |
Gotchas:
- Only exports requested by the caller are returned.
- The response contains no download URL; tell the user to download from LPM Settings.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors.
Pairs with: `create_export_request`, `list_notifications`

### `create_export_request` [O] · write · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Queues a background job that packages all data of a workspace or of one project into a JSON zip for download in the LPM web app.
Use when: The user explicitly asks for a backup or full data export of a workspace or project.    Avoid when: You only need some records: use the matching list_/get_ tools.; You need analytics: use get_project_analytics or get_operational_analytics.; An export for the same scope is already queued or running (check list_export_requests).
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| scope | yes | constant | workspace \| project |
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Required when scope = workspace. |
| projectId | no | list_projects -> id | Required when scope = project. |
| filters | no | user | Object; stored but currently ignored (the export is always complete). |
Preconditions: scope workspace: caller is the workspace owner or an active member.; scope project: caller can read the project.; API key profile includes sensitive admin tools (full or custom).; The user explicitly asked for the export.
Returns: Export request object {id, status: 'queued', scope, workspaceId, projectId, format: 'json-zip', createdAt, ...}. Track it with list_export_requests.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'Workspace export requires a workspace' | Pass workspaceId with scope workspace. |
| 'Project export requires a project' | Pass projectId with scope project. |
| 'You do not have access to this workspace' | The caller is not an active member. Ask the workspace owner. |
| 'Project <id> not found' / 'You do not have access to this project' | Check projectId with list_projects; ask for access if needed. |
Gotchas:
- Asynchronous: poll list_export_requests until status is completed or failed.
- On completion the requester gets a notification ('Export concluído') and webhooks subscribed to export.completed fire.
- The zip holds ALL data of the scope (flagged in the catalog as a data exfiltration risk); filters are stored but ignored by the export job.
- Each call queues a new full export.
- No download link via MCP: the user downloads it from LPM Settings.
Pairs with: `list_export_requests`, `list_notifications`

### `get_analytics_bridge_observability` [A] · read · portfolio:read · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Shows the state of the analytics export pipeline (Firestore -> Cloud Storage NDJSON -> BigQuery) for a workspace or project: runtime config, run counts, recent runs and per-entity watermarks.
Use when: User asks whether analytics exports/BigQuery loads are healthy; Before creating a new analytics bridge run, to see if one is already queued or failed    Avoid when: You only need the list of runs: use list_analytics_bridge_runs; You need delivery metrics: use get_project_analytics
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Send workspaceId or projectId (at least one). |
| projectId | no | list_projects -> id | If given, it wins and the workspace is derived from the project. |
Preconditions: At least one of workspaceId/projectId is given; Caller can read that workspace or project
Returns: {scope{workspaceId, projectId}, generatedAt, runtime{datasetId, bucketName, bigQueryLoadEnabled, bigQueryProjectId}, stats{queued, running, completed, failed, lastCompletedAt, lastFailedAt}, watermarks:[{entityType, cursorField, cursorValue, lastSuccessfulRunId, lastSuccessfulAt}], recentRuns:[run objects, max 15]}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Analytics bridge observability requires workspaceId or projectId | Send one of them. |
| You do not have access to this project / workspace | Stop and ask the user for access. |
Gotchas:
- stats and recentRuns include ONLY runs created by the calling user.
- Watermarks are per exact scope (workspace scope and project scope are separate).
- bigQueryLoadEnabled=false means runs only write NDJSON files.
- Output contains infrastructure names (bucket, dataset): do not share outside the team.
Pairs with: `list_analytics_bridge_runs`, `create_analytics_bridge_run`

### `list_analytics_bridge_runs` [A] · read · portfolio:read · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the caller's own recent analytics bridge runs, newest first, optionally filtered by workspace or project.
Use when: You need a runId to process or inspect; Checking the status/error of runs you created    Avoid when: You need pipeline health and watermarks: use get_analytics_bridge_observability
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Exact-match filter on the run's workspaceId (also matches project-scope runs of that workspace). |
| projectId | no | list_projects -> id | Exact-match filter on the run's projectId. |
Preconditions: Authenticated caller
Returns: Array (max 20) of {id, workspaceId, projectId, status queued|running|completed|failed|canceled, mode, entityTypes, resetEntities, requestedReason, exportedRows, storagePrefix, loadJobs, createdAt, startedAt, completedAt, failedAt, errorMessage}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Empty array | The caller has created no runs in that scope; runs of other users are never shown. |
Gotchas:
- Only runs requested by the caller; no pagination (max 20).
Pairs with: `process_analytics_bridge_run`, `get_analytics_bridge_observability`

### `create_analytics_bridge_run` [C] · write · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Queues a new analytics export run (status 'queued') for a workspace or project; it does not execute it.
Use when: The user explicitly asks to export/refresh analytics data to Storage/BigQuery    Avoid when: A queued run already exists in list_analytics_bridge_runs: process it with process_analytics_bridge_run instead; User only wants to read metrics: use get_project_analytics
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Send workspaceId or projectId (at least one). |
| projectId | no | list_projects -> id | If given, workspace is derived from the project. |
| entityTypes | no | constant | Array from audit_events\|issues\|requirements\|projects\|delivery_health_daily\|team_delivery_health_daily. Omit for all six. Send only these values. |
| mode | no | constant | incremental (default) \| backfill. |
| resetEntities | no | constant | Subset of entityTypes to re-export from scratch; others are dropped. |
| requestedReason | no | user | Free text explaining why. |
Preconditions: At least one of workspaceId/projectId is given; Caller can read that workspace or project (only read access is checked); User asked for the export
Returns: Run object {id, status:'queued', mode, entityTypes, resetEntities, storagePrefix, workspaceId, projectId, createdAt}; use id as runId in process_analytics_bridge_run.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Analytics bridge run requires workspaceId or projectId | Send one of them. |
| You do not have access to this project / workspace | Stop and ask the user for access. |
Gotchas:
- No background worker processes queued runs (runAnalyticsBridgeWorkerCycle exists but nothing calls it): the run stays 'queued' until process_analytics_bridge_run is called.
- Creating a run resets the watermark cursor of each selected entity to null, so the next processing re-exports everything even in 'incremental' mode, and BigQuery loads append rows (duplicates).
Pairs with: `get_analytics_bridge_observability`, `process_analytics_bridge_run`, `list_analytics_bridge_runs`

### `process_analytics_bridge_run` [C] · destructive · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Synchronously executes a queued analytics run: collects scope data, writes NDJSON files to Cloud Storage, upserts daily delivery-health records, loads BigQuery when enabled, advances watermarks and marks the run completed or failed.
Use when: Right after create_analytics_bridge_run, when the user wants the export executed; A run created by the same user is stuck in 'queued'    Avoid when: The run was created by another user: never process it (ask them); The run status is completed/failed: processing is a no-op; create a new run only if the user asks; You only need status: use list_analytics_bridge_runs
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| runId | yes | create_analytics_bridge_run -> id or list_analytics_bridge_runs -> [].id |  |
Preconditions: Run exists with status 'queued'; Run was created by the caller (enforced by the web route but NOT by the MCP handler); User asked for the export
Returns: Run object {id, status completed|failed (or unchanged if it was not queued), exportedRows, loadJobs{<entity>:{status loaded|skipped|failed, errorMessage}}, watermarks, completedAt, failedAt, errorMessage}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32602 Analytics bridge run not found | Re-check runId with list_analytics_bridge_runs. |
| Returned run has status 'failed' and errorMessage | Report errorMessage to the user; do not loop or create new runs automatically. |
| Returned status still 'queued' or 'running' | Another process holds it or it was not queued; wait and check list_analytics_bridge_runs. |
Gotchas:
- Long synchronous call: reads every issue/requirement in scope and the whole audit_events collection; may exceed connector timeouts (~60 s).
- Exported files and appended BigQuery rows cannot be undone from LPM.
- Returns normally (no error) when the run was not queued; check status and startedAt.
Pairs with: `create_analytics_bridge_run`, `get_analytics_bridge_observability`

### `list_workspaces` [A] · read · workspace:read · owner `lpm-start` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the workspaces the caller can reach, to obtain workspaceId.
Use when: First step of almost any task: find the workspaceId by name.; Checking whether you can manage a workspace (API key: access.canManage).    Avoid when: You already have the workspaceId and need its details: use get_workspace.; You need the projects: use list_workspace_projects or list_projects.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| teamId | no | list_teams -> id | API key only; OAuth rejects it as unknown_field. |
| status | no | constant | active \| archived. |
| compact | no | constant | true returns only id, name, key, status, teamId, ownerId, createdAt, updatedAt (drops access.canManage). |
| limit | no | constant | Max number returned. OAuth: integer 1-100. |
Preconditions: OAuth: scope workspace:read.
Returns: API key: array (newest first) of workspace records {id, name, slug, description, status, ownerId, teamId, createdAt, updatedAt, access:{canManage}}. OAuth: [{id, name}] of authorized active workspaces only.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| OAuth -32602 invalid_arguments (unknown_field teamId, or limit out of range) | Under OAuth send only status, compact, limit (1-100). |
| -32003 access denied | Call get_mcp_connection_info to see the connection's scopes. |
Gotchas:
- access.canManage=true (owner/admin) is required for update_workspace, delete_workspace_issue_link and update_workspace_ai_config.
- With an API key the list also includes workspaces where you only own a project; get_workspace may then deny access.
- OAuth: status 'archived' always returns [] and a single-workspace grant returns only that workspace.
- Use compact:true to save context only when you do not need canManage.
Pairs with: `get_mcp_connection_info`, `get_workspace`, `list_workspace_projects`

### `list_workspace_projects` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-start` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the projects of a workspace (archived ones excluded unless requested).
Use when: Finding a projectId inside a known workspace.; Mapping the projects of a workspace before creating cross-project links.    Avoid when: You also want to filter by team or prefer the shared listing used by the CLI ('lpm projects list --workspace-id'): use list_projects.; You need one project's details: use get_project.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id |  |
| includeArchived | no | constant | Boolean, default false. |
Preconditions: The caller is the workspace owner or an active member (project-only or team-only access is denied).; OAuth: scope portfolio:read and the workspace in the grant.
Returns: JSON array of full project records {id, name, key, description, workspaceId, teamId, ownerId, archived, ...}. id is the projectId.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32602 'You do not have access to this workspace' | You are not a workspace member; try list_projects (also returns projects you reach via team/ownership) or ask the owner. |
| OAuth -32003 | The workspace is outside the grant; call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- Returns full project records (can be large), unordered, no pagination.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `get_project`, `list_issues`

### `list_workspace_members` [A] · read · workspace:read · owner `lpm-workspace-admin` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the members of a workspace with their roles.
Use when: You need the userId, email or role of people in a workspace.; You must confirm the caller is owner/admin before using admin tools.; Choosing accountableOwnerUserId (role owner/admin) for agent principals or credentials.; Before add_workspace_member, to avoid adding someone twice.    Avoid when: Who can be assigned activities in one project: use list_project_assignable_members.; Team members: use list_team_members.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | On a single-workspace OAuth grant it may be omitted; the grant fills it in. |
Preconditions: The caller is the workspace owner or an active member.
Returns: JSON array of {id (= userId), workspaceId, userId, userEmail, role (owner|admin|member|viewer), status, createdAt, updatedAt}.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32602 'You do not have access to this workspace' | Wrong workspaceId or caller is not a member; re-check list_workspaces. |
| OAuth -32003 access denied | Workspace is outside the grant; call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- The owner is also stored in the workspace document (get_workspace -> ownerId) and keeps full rights from it.
- Only owner/admin can manage (WORKSPACE_ADMIN_ROLES); member and viewer are read-only. No pagination.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `get_user`, `add_workspace_member`, `remove_workspace_member`

### `get_project_analytics` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-review-health` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns delivery-health metrics for one project: 30-day throughput, lead/cycle/blocked times, open blocked issues with what blocks them, completion rate, health status and data-integrity signals.
Use when: User asks how a project is performing, its delivery health, throughput or lead time; You need the currently blocked issues of a project together with the issues that block them (projects[0].blockedIssues); You need data-integrity signals (orphan AISH jobs, stale active cycles, invalid statuses)    Avoid when: You need metrics for one cycle: cycleId is ignored; use get_cycle and list_issues for that cycle instead; You need the executive view with risks, finance and decisions: use get_project_owner_surface; You need intake/operational-entry metrics: use get_operational_analytics; You need dependency chains: use get_project_dependency_summary
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id (or list_workspace_projects -> id) | Project must not be archived. |
| cycleId | no | list_cycles -> id | Declared but IGNORED by the server; do not rely on it. |
Preconditions: Project exists and is not archived; Caller can read the project
Returns: {scope, generatedAt, metrics:{issuesCount, completedIssues, throughput30d, avgLeadTimeDays, avgCycleTimeDays, avgRequirementLeadTimeDays, avgBlockedTimeDays, blockedIssuesOpen, completionRate (percent 0-100), healthStatus healthy|watch|critical, integrity{status healthy|watch|critical, signals[], invalidIssueStatuses, staleActiveCycles, orphanAishJobs, orphanAutopilotIssues, terminalIssueJobMismatches, requirementsUpdatedAfterCurrentBaseline, details{orphanAishJobs[], terminalIssueJobMismatches[]} ({jobId, category missing-linked-issue|unclassified-standalone-job|completed-job-open-issue|done-issue-nonterminal-job, reason})}}, projects:[{projectId, projectName, throughput30d, blockedIssuesOpen, blockedIssues:[{issueId, title, status, blockedSince, blockedBy:[{issueId, title}], reason}], completedIssues, totalIssues, integrity}]}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this project | Project is archived or not visible to the caller. Check list_projects (with archived included) and ask the owner for access; do not retry. |
| -32003 or OAuth access denied | Tool is API-key only (no OAuth scope). Call get_mcp_connection_info and tell the user. |
Gotchas:
- Catalog description promises velocity/burndown/status distribution but the server returns delivery-health metrics.
- cycleId is ignored: the handler passes only projectId.
- Archived projects return an access error.
- Result is cached about 10 s per server instance.
Pairs with: `list_projects`, `list_blocked_project_issues`, `get_project_dependency_summary`
